edges.rationale: The JPEG lives directly inside apps/frontend/src/assets/avatar/ as one of its contents.
Sibling avatar in the same directory.
Sibling avatar in the same directory.
Profile.jsx reads uploaded avatar files from this directory before persisting them as data URLs on the user object.
Both pages invoke userAPI.updateProfile to save the avatar, with Profile handling the cropper and Settings handling the simple upload.
Profile.jsx sets user.avatar (defined on the User type) by calling userAPI.updateProfile after cropping.
Settings.jsx calls userAPI.updateProfile({avatar: reader.result}) to overwrite the avatar field on the User type.
Navbar reads user.avatar to render the header avatar image.
BottomNav reads user.avatar to render the mobile bottom nav avatar.
TestInterface renders user.avatar (or user.avatarUrl) next to the test taker.
TestReview displays user.avatar in the result review screen.
Dashboard reads performer.avatar (the same shape as user.avatar) on the leaderboard cards.
Navbar can fall back to LOCAL_ASSETS.defaultAvatar / getAvatarUrl when user.avatar is missing.
BottomNav can fall back to the same default avatar helper when no avatar is set.
StudyMaterialChapter uses ui-avatars.com which follows the same fallback-avatar pattern as getAvatarUrl in assets-config.js.
TestDetails renders rank.avatar, which is the same avatar field as user.avatar on the shared User type.
The timestamped filename pattern in this directory is the evidence behind the Avatar Asset Strategy rationale.
